Cleaned up `prompt.md`. Key changes and why:

- **Removed a direct contradiction**: the old prompt required "exactly two paragraphs" (line 20) and "exactly three paragraphs" (line 26) — this is almost certainly a chunk of why the model was ignoring parts of the prompt (it can't satisfy both, so it likely guessed or dropped one).
- **Dropped the "Delivery reminder" table**: it repeated the citation-placement rule verbatim and buried one new rule (acronym expansion) at the very bottom — folded the acronym rule into the main rules list and removed the duplicate.
- **Removed stylistic asks that don't fit a factual internal tool**: "friendly sign-off," "memorable analogy," "suggest a related topic." These read like consumer-chatbot flourishes competing with the factual/citation-heavy tone the rest of the prompt demands — likely another source of inconsistent output. Flagging this explicitly in case you actually want them back.
- **Toned down "PROTECT CONFIDENTIALITY!!!"**: shouting/emphasis-heavy text doesn't make Claude more compliant, it just adds noise. Merged it with the phone-number rule into one concrete redaction instruction.
- **Moved `{{retrieved_documents}}` to the top**, wrapped in `<retrieved_documents>` tags: for long variable context, placing it before the instructions (rather than sandwiched in the middle) improves grounding, and keeps the rules positioned right before the model has to act.
- **Flagged one undefined term**: "escalation age limit" was never defined anywhere in the original prompt. I turned it into an explicit `{{escalation_age_limit}}` template variable to match the existing `{{retrieved_documents}}` pattern — confirm your calling code actually populates it, otherwise define a fixed value instead.

Net effect: shorter, no contradictions, no duplicate instructions, and the model's attention is aimed at the rules right before it answers.
